questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Fourier Series?
questions.answer: A Fourier series represents a periodic signal as a constant term plus sine and cosine harmonics. Each harmonic is a simple wave mode with an integer multiple of the fundamental frequency.

questions.prompt: What does \(x\) mean in Fourier Series?
questions.answer: In Fourier Series, \(x\) means dimensionless input on an interval of length 2 pi.

questions.prompt: Identify another important piece of notation used in Fourier Series.

questions.prompt: State a central formula or test for Fourier Series.
questions.answer:
The fourier series is
\[f(x)\sim\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(a_n\cos nx+b_n\sin nx)\]
Use it only after the symbols in the formula have been identified for the specific fourier series problem.

questions.prompt: Write the Fourier series for f(x)=3 cos 2x.
questions.answer: The function already is one Fourier mode. The constant coefficient is zero, every sine coefficient is zero, and every cosine coefficient is zero except a_2=3. Therefore \[f(x)=3\cos2x\] is its own Fourier series.
